title: Aurora Analytics - Health & Cost Review (Q1)
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage spike in Jan, cost increase from embeddings batch, reliability incident review, and alignment on roadmap items (per-route dashboards, caching optimizations). Action items: Redwood to send cost breakdown and proposed autoscale tweaks; Aurora to provide specific eval prompts and SOC2 auditor contact.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Olivia (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Janelle (Aurora Head of MLOps), Marcus (Platform Eng), Priya (Finance), Ethan (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): medium quality transcription. Topics: Q1 usage/costs, reliability incident 2025-01-27, roadmap features, security docs.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samir here, Olivia and Ravi from Redwood. Janelle, Marcus, Priya, Ethan you there?
[00:08] Janelle (Aurora): Yep, here. Thanks for doing this. We wanted to get ahead of some cost questions from finance and also go over the incident last month.
[00:15] Olivia (Redwood-SE): Hi all, I have the usage graphs up — I'll walk through the Jan to Feb delta.
[00:20] Marcus (Aurora): Also curious about dedicated pool options, since we saw tail latency spikes during forecast jobs.
[00:28] Samir: Great — plan is: Olivia will do numbers, Ravi will cover adoption/health, then we'll talk next steps and security.

--- Topics: Usage and cost ---
[00:50] Olivia: Okay, um, weekly tokens for December were around 1.2 billion tokens, we saw a 40% increase in January with the new embeddings pipeline — that accounts for most of the cost uptick. The big driver was the batch embedding job that re-embedded the 12M vector corpus, and at the default sharded batch size it created more calls than expected.
[01:20] Priya (Finance): To be clear: our bill in Jan was 63% higher than Dec, and CFO wants either optimizations or a reserved capacity quote.
[01:28] Samir: We can provide both. One immediate lever is batching and caching — Olivia, remind the group about automatic prefix and KV cache recommendations?
[01:35] Olivia: Sure. So Redwood automatically caches prefix results for chat flows and we have an optional KV cache for embeddings reuse. For the Aurora embedding re-run, we suggest increasing local batch sizes and enabling per-shard caching — that reduces duplicated tokenization and RPC. In our test envs that drops token-cost by ~30% for similar workloads, but note it can increase memory usage on the serving nodes.
[02:02] Ethan (SRE): Memory is constrained on our side; we run smaller GPU types in prod. How would the memory bump look?
[02:08] Olivia: It depends — quantized models and smaller sequence length help. We can simulate with your sequence length histogram. If you share that we'll run a quick projection.
[02:20] Marcus: Also we saw latency tail spikes during the 2am daily jobs — is that a concurrency issue?
[02:26] Olivia: Likely a batching/backpressure issue. If a big scheduled job floods the host, other requests see increased queuing. Dedicated capacity or rate-limiting background jobs can mitigate. There's also our burst policy for Dedicated which isolates scheduled batch lanes.

--- Topics: Reliability incident (2025-01-27) ---
[03:05] Ravi (Redwood-CSM): Quick recap of the Jan 27th incident — Aurora reported a 15-minute window where gen requests returned 503s intermittently. We traced to a degraded network link in region-us-west-2 which caused router failover and a capacity imbalance. We failed open in a way that increased queueing rather than gracefully rejecting low-priority jobs.
[03:35] Janelle: From our side, the impact was mostly on internal staging and the forecasting pipeline. Production customer-facing features had graceful fallbacks but it still triggered on-call.
[03:45] Ethan: We saw retry storms which made it worse. Need guidance on backoff recommendations.
[03:50] Samir: Agreed — proposed fixes: 1) apply stricter circuit-breaker defaults in your SDK client (we'll share config), 2) Redwood will update routing policy so canary UX and background jobs are deprioritized during node pressure, 3) add more granular alerting to catch queue length before 503s.
[04:20] Janelle: Sounds good. Can you put those auto-retry/backoff configs in writing? We need the ops playbook.
[04:25] Samir: Yes, action item.

--- Topics: Pricing and reserved capacity ---
[05:00] Priya: For reserved capacity, what's the typical discount and commitment? And if we need burst beyond reserved, how are we billed?
[05:12] Samir: Reserved pricing depends on GPU class and commit term. Typical discounts are in the 30-45% range for 12-month commits. Bursts are charged at on-demand rates; we can structure a hybrid where you get a predictable base for ETL and a burst pool for spikes. We'll send an initial commercial summary.
[05:30] Priya: Please include an example monthly P&L showing token price delta if we move 40% of embedding runs to Dedicated.
[05:35] Samir: Can do. We'll also include a migration runbook.

--- Topics: Security & compliance ---
[06:05] Janelle: On security: our auditor has asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence, SAML SSO logs, and KMS integration details. We've been asked if Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
[06:18] Olivia: For Hosted we have server-side encryption and we integrate with KMS for Dedicated and Private. Customer-managed keys are supported on Private. We will attach SOC2 summary and SSO SAML docs after the call.
[06:30] Marcus: Also need more verbose audit logs for token-level access traceability — can Redwood increase retention for a snapshot we keep for 90 days?
[06:38] Ravi: Yes, we have an observability add-on for extended retention and per-route tracing; we'll provide pricing and retention SLA.

--- Topics: Roadmap alignment ---
[07:05] Olivia: Roadmap items relevant to Aurora: per-route dashboards (coming in Q2), smarter caching/auto-batching improvements (Q3 alpha), and Optimize tool suggestions for quantization. We can prioritize per-route windowing if you want earlier access.
[07:25] Janelle: Per-route dashboards would solve a lot of our triage overhead. Is there a beta program?
[07:30] Samir: Yes — we can on-board you to an early access cohort. That will include a short integration and weekly syncs.
[07:38] Priya: Any non-functional changes that could immediately reduce cost?
[07:42] Olivia: Short term: change embedding job batch size, enable KV reuse, lower sampling temperature for certain internal pipelines to reduce generation length. Mid term: move long-running ETL to Dedicated reserved nodes.

--- Transcript noise / mis-hears (typical) ---
[08:05] Marcus: When you say K-V cash — I thought that was a KMS thing, sorry I heard it wrong.
[08:09] Olivia: K-V cache — it's a small key-value layer for reusing embeddings. Not KMS.

--- Q&A and clarifications ---
[08:30] Ethan: If we go Dedicated, what does the onboarding timeline look like?
[08:34] Samir: For a standard Dedicated cluster it's roughly 4-8 weeks depending on procurement and capacity class. Private on-prem is longer — typically 8-12 weeks because of network / security reviews.
[08:45] Janelle: We might try a hybrid: reserve for ETL and keep low-latency hosted for product traffic. Is there a way to route by traffic class?
[08:52] Olivia: Yes, routing policies can split by route, model, or label. You can pin product traffic to hosted instances and ETL to Dedicated. We also support automatic fallback if pinned pool is saturated.

--- Action Items recapped mid-call ---
[09:05] Ravi: I'll log action items — Samir to send pricing and migration runbook; Olivia to run a cost projection with Aurora's sequence length histogram; Redwood to share SOC2 and SAML docs; Aurora to share auditor contact and the exact eval prompt set.

[09:20] Priya: When can we expect the cost projection? CFO wants it before next week.
[09:24] Samir: We can aim for EOD Thursday (2025-02-16) for an initial projection.

--- Deeper technical nitty-gritty (SE-led) ---
[10:05] Olivia: Marcus, can you share the sequence hist and the embedding job config? For embeddings, we saw a few customers where vectorizing long docs without chunking led to large token spikes. Chunking + overlap reduced tokens per doc by 45% without losing recall.
[10:30] Marcus: We'll provide the config. Also, any recommendations for model quantization? We're using a 16-bit variant now but thinking of int8.
[10:38] Olivia: int8 is solid for embeddings; for generation you want to validate on prompt sets. Redwood Optimize will surface model/quant recommendations, but we can run a brief eval on your test set.

--- Customers objections and tradeoffs ---
[11:05] Priya: Cost savings sound good, but we're cautious about Dedicated because of vendor lock-in and management overhead.
[11:12] Samir: Understood. That's why hybrid is common — commit to a baseline, keep burst on hosted, and we provide migration automation so you can revert.
[11:20] Janelle: Another concern is data residency for EU customers — will Private solve that?
[11:25] Olivia: Yes, Private (VPC/on-prem) and regional dedicated capacity can meet residency needs. We'll include our region map and data flow docs.

--- Closing: recap & next steps ---
[12:00] Samir: Quick recap — action items and owners: we'll send pricing + example P&L, run the cost projection with your sequence hist, share SOC2/SAML/KMS docs, and slot you into per-route dashboard beta if you confirm.
[12:18] Janelle: Confirmed — please send the docs, and we'll share the histogram and auditor contact.
[12:24] Priya: Once we have a P&L we may request an internal exec briefing.
[12:28] Samir: We'll prepare an exec-friendly summary. Ravi will schedule a follow-up next week.

[12:35] Ravi: I'll send calendar invites for two follow-ups: one technical deep-dive (Olivia + Marcus) and one finance exec briefing (Samir + Priya).
[12:42] Ethan: Thanks, all.
[12:45] Samir: Thanks everyone; end of call.
